title: What is prompt injection? When an email tries to give orders
description: Recognize when outside text tries to redirect an AI agent. Follow a delivery-email example and see how read-only access and send approvals limit the damage.
keywords: indirect prompt injection in ai agents
answer: **prompt injection happens when someone puts instructions into text an ai reads to steer it away from your task.** an email you asked it to summarize can tell it to do something else. if the bot mistakes that request for yours, it might give a false answer or act with your permissions.

review.by: lead agent, after four independent reviewers read every page against seo/facts (2026-11-20); every finding applied

og_line: an email cannot give itself permission.
definition: prompt injection is an attempt to make an ai follow instructions from someone who has no authority over its task.
example: **loretta wants the delivery window from a warehouse email.** in this example, the email also asks her assistant to send back the staff rota. a useful answer gives the delivery window and flags the unrelated request. the warehouse can request the rota. only loretta can decide to share it.

sections.h: look for the change of job
sections.md:
**compare the request with what you actually asked.** finding a delivery time takes no staff records. an official-looking signature adds no authority. the same problem can crop up in a web page that a bot reads for you.

outside text can also distort a summary without asking for a send. for an important delivery, compare the time in the answer with the original line.

sections.h: limit what the bot can do in dusk bot
sections.md:
**give a bot that reads mail read only access to the connected app.** dusk bot blocks actions that would change things through that connection. leave unrelated apps off for that bot.[^1]

sends through connected apps ask first by default. if a request arrives, compare the recipient and the material with your original task. deny a send you never requested.[^1][^2]

careful with **Full access**: a bot there with no sending rule can send up to 25 a day without asking. give it **Ask every time**.

sections.h: when to open the message yourself
sections.md: **read the original yourself if you need to rule out a misleading summary.** dusk bot's send controls give you a decision about an outgoing action. they cannot tell you whether the delivery time in a reply is true.

faq.q: does the instruction have to be hidden?
faq.a: no. a perfectly visible request can mislead an agent. the question is who authorized the work, even when the wording seems ordinary.

faq.q: what does indirect prompt injection mean?
faq.a: the instruction reaches the agent through something it reads, such as a web page or an attachment. you can encounter it while asking a perfectly ordinary question.
